---
title: "Unit Testing"
description: "Testing a small, isolated unit of software to check that it behaves as expected."
term: "Unit Testing"
letter: "U"
category: "Software Engineering"
difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

Unit testing checks a small piece of code, such as a function, with
controlled inputs and expected outputs. It helps catch regressions early
and makes component behavior easier to understand.

## Technical explanation

A unit test exercises a narrowly scoped component, often using fixtures,
assertions, and mocks or fakes for external dependencies. Tests should be
deterministic and independent where practical; integration and end-to-end
tests cover interactions that unit tests do not.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

AI applications include ordinary software logic around models, including
preprocessing, schema handling, scoring, and tool execution. Unit tests can
verify these deterministic behaviors, while model quality requires
separate data-driven evaluation.

## How it works

A test supplies known inputs, invokes the unit, and compares outputs or
side effects with expectations. Edge cases and invalid inputs should be
included. Model-dependent behavior may need statistical or benchmark
tests rather than brittle exact-output assertions.

## Practical example

A preprocessing function can be tested to ensure that missing fields are
handled consistently and that output tensors have the expected shape.
Separately, a model evaluation suite checks predictive quality on a
representative dataset.

## Common misconceptions

- Passing unit tests does not establish that a model is accurate, fair, or
  safe in deployment.
- Mocking every dependency can hide integration errors; tests at multiple
  levels are useful.
